ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Layer-wise cosine of text and image gradients in a 1.5B autoregressive unified model
PROPOSAL: Train a 1.5B decoder with a 16384-entry VQ image tokenizer on interleaved text and image-caption data for 20B tokens, saving 5 checkpoints. At the checkpoints, draw 200 mini-batches, back-propagate the text loss and the image loss separately and calculate the cosine between the two gradients for attention and feed-forward weights. Report mean and spread across batches by layer.
CONTROLS: Two random halves of the text data as a conflict-free baseline; two halves of the image data; shuffled image-caption pairing.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Cosine is near zero or negative in early and late layers and closer to positive in the middle, while the baseline stays high. It could fail if small batches obscure the differences in noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Per-head gradient conflict profile in a 1.5B autoregressive unified model over training
PROPOSAL: Train a 1.5B decoder with a 16384-entry VQ image tokenizer on interleaved data for 40B tokens, saving 10 checkpoints. At the checkpoints, draw 500 mini-batches, back-propagate the text loss and the image loss separately and calculate the cosine between gradients per layer, per attention head and per feed-forward block. Report mean and spread over batches, the share of batches with negative cosine, and the correlation between head-level and layer-level values.
CONTROLS: Two random halves of the text data; two halves of the image data; shuffled image-caption pairing.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Head-level cosines spread widely within a layer yet average to the layer-level trend, with conflict peaking in a few heads. It could fail if head-level estimates are too noisy to rank.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Modality-specific normalisation and scaling in a shared 1.5B transformer
PROPOSAL: Train a 1.5B shared autoregressive transformer from scratch on 150B tokens of text and image-text pairs with a 16384-entry VQ tokenizer, with and without modality-conditioned layer-norm gains and biases in the blocks, using 2 seeds. Evaluate validation loss per modality, GenEval and DPG-Bench for generation, and MMBench and POPE for understanding.
CONTROLS: A shared-normalisation baseline; separate feed-forward experts per modality as an upper reference; a loss-reweighting baseline that rescales the image loss by 0.5.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: The design lowers image validation loss by 2 to 4 percent at equal tokens and matches the experts within 1 point on GenEval. It could fail if normalisation alone cannot remove the conflict.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Modality-conditioned residual scaling in a 1.5B shared transformer over a longer schedule
PROPOSAL: Train a 1.5B shared autoregressive transformer from scratch on 300B tokens of text and image-text pairs with a 16384-entry VQ tokenizer, with and without learned per-modality scalars on the residual branches, using 3 seeds. Evaluate validation loss per modality, GenEval, MMBench and POPE, keeping the learning rate and warm-up identical in both arms.
CONTROLS: A shared baseline; a loss-reweighting baseline that rescales the image loss by 0.5.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Per-modality scalars lower image validation loss by 1 to 3 percent and keep MMBench within 1 point. It could fail if gains disappear at the end of the longer schedule.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Codebook size and image-token statistics as drivers of modality conflict
PROPOSAL: Train 3 tokenizers with codebook sizes 4096, 16384 and 65536, then train 0.5B decoders on the same data for 30B tokens each, using 2 seeds. Measure token entropy and n-gram predictability of the image-token sequences and the per-layer gradient cosine between text and image losses, and correlate the statistics with conflict.
CONTROLS: A variant where image tokens are randomly permuted so spatial statistics vanish; shuffled image-caption pairing.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Larger codebooks raise entropy and deepen negative cosine in the middle layers, and the permuted variant removes most of the conflict. It could fail if conflict tracks data volume rather than token statistics.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Raster-order and token-statistics probes of modality conflict at 0.5B
PROPOSAL: Train 0.5B decoders with a 16384-entry codebook, with image tokens in raster, Hilbert-curve or random-column order, for 60B tokens and 5 seeds, using the same learning rate, batch size and data order over orderings. Measure the per-layer gradient cosine between text and image losses and the mutual information between neighbouring image tokens. Report image loss and caption loss.
CONTROLS: A variant with randomly permuted image tokens; shuffled image-caption pairing.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Orderings with higher neighbour information give less negative cosine in the middle layers. It could fail if ordering changes the loss without changing the conflict.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gradient projection against modality-aware norms in a 0.5B model
PROPOSAL: Compare PCGrad-style projection of conflicting text and image gradients with modality-conditioned layer norms in a 0.5B model trained from scratch on 20B tokens, with 3 seeds. Report validation loss per modality, GenEval score and wall-clock per step.
CONTROLS: A plain shared baseline; loss reweighting; a random projection that removes a gradient component of equal norm.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Norms match projection on loss at lower step time, which is 15 to 25 percent faster. It could fail if projection fixes conflicts that norms leave in the early layers.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Five conflict-handling optimisers compared on a 0.5B autoregressive model
PROPOSAL: Train 0.5B models on 20B tokens with PCGrad, GradDrop, CAGrad, MGDA and plain summation of the text and image losses, with 3 seeds. Report validation loss per modality, GenEval score, step time and the fraction of steps where a conflict is detected.
CONTROLS: A shared baseline with a tuned learning rate; loss reweighting; a random projection of equal norm.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: All projection methods reduce image loss by under 2 percent and cost 15 to 30 percent more per step. It could fail if conflicts detected per step are too rare to matter.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training efficiency of the modality-aware design at three model sizes
PROPOSAL: Train baseline and design variants at 0.5B, 1.5B and 3B on matched 100B-token budgets, with 3 seeds at 0.5B and fewer seeds at the larger sizes. Fit loss-against-tokens curves and report the tokens needed to reach a shared validation loss per modality.
CONTROLS: The baseline; a parameter-matched larger baseline; a learning-rate sweep over 3 values on the baseline.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: The design reaches the shared loss with 15 to 25 percent fewer tokens at all sizes. It could fail if the advantage shrinks as size grows.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Final-loss comparison of baseline and modality-aware 3B models with repeated seeds
PROPOSAL: Train baseline and design variants at 3B on 200B tokens, with 3 seeds for both. Report final validation loss per modality, GenEval with 8 sampling seeds, DPG-Bench and MMBench, log the loss curve at 1000-step intervals and give a difference between the two arms over 1000 bootstrap resamples, at 4 checkpoints.
CONTROLS: The baseline; a parameter-matched larger baseline; a learning-rate sweep over 3 values on the baseline.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: The design lowers final image loss by 2 to 3 percent with a confidence interval excluding zero. It could fail if seed spread is as large as the difference.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Probing a public 7B autoregressive unified checkpoint for layer-wise conflict
PROPOSAL: Load the public Chameleon-7B checkpoint and draw 300 mini-batches of 16 text sequences and 16 image-caption sequences tokenised from CC12M captions. Back-propagate the text loss and image loss separately and calculate the cosine between the gradients for attention and feed-forward weights in the layers, with a LoRA-only repeat to check agreement.
CONTROLS: Two random halves of the text data; shuffled image-caption pairing; a different seed for the batch draw.
COST: 64
PREDICTION: Cosine is lowest in layers 10 to 20 of 32 and agrees between full and LoRA measurements within 0.05. It could fail if the checkpoint's instruction tuning masks pretraining conflict.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Layer-wise probe of a public 7B checkpoint at three data mixtures
PROPOSAL: Load the public Chameleon-7B checkpoint and draw 500 mini-batches from the 3 mixtures: CC12M captions, VQA pairs and editing instructions. Back-propagate the text loss and image loss separately and calculate the cosine between gradients per layer and per attention head, using 16 sequences per modality and the checkpoint's own image tokenizer.
CONTROLS: Two random halves of the text data; shuffled image-caption pairing.
COST: 64
PREDICTION: The middle layers show the lowest cosine in all 3 mixtures, deeper for editing. It could fail if mixtures differ mainly in sequence length.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Pretraining a 3B autoregressive unified model with modality-aware blocks
PROPOSAL: Train a 3B decoder from scratch on 400B tokens of text, captions, VQA and editing pairs, using modality-conditioned norms and per-modality low-rank adapters in the middle layers. Evaluate GenEval, DPG-Bench, MMBench, POPE, MME and ImgEdit, and log the per-layer gradient cosine at 4 checkpoints.
CONTROLS: A shared 3B baseline on the same tokens; a baseline with parameters matched to the adapters; the middle-layer adapters removed.
COST: 3200
PREDICTION: The design beats the shared baseline by 2 to 4 points on GenEval and 1 to 2 points on MMBench. It could fail if adapters help generation at the cost of understanding.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A 3B autoregressive unified model with modality-conditioned norms on a longer schedule
PROPOSAL: Train a 3B decoder from scratch on 600B tokens of text, captions, VQA and editing pairs with modality-conditioned norms, using 3 seeds and the same data order and learning-rate schedule in both models. Evaluate GenEval, DPG-Bench, MMBench, POPE, MME, ImgEdit, GQA and TextVQA at 8 checkpoints.
CONTROLS: A shared 3B baseline on the same tokens; a baseline with parameters matched to the norms.
COST: 3200
PREDICTION: The design beats the baseline by 1 to 3 points on GenEval at the final checkpoint. It could fail if early gains vanish with longer training.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Benchmark evaluation of trained checkpoints on five generation and understanding sets
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the baseline and design 1.5B checkpoints on GenEval, DPG-Bench, MMBench, POPE and ImgEdit. Use 4 sampling seeds for generation and greedy decoding for understanding, and report scores with bootstrap intervals over prompts.
CONTROLS: A public 1B reference model; the baseline checkpoint; a checkpoint from the middle of training.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: Design scores exceed the baseline by 1 to 3 points on generation sets, with understanding scores within 1 point. It could fail if sampling seeds alone move scores by that much.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Broad evaluation of three 1.5B checkpoints on nine benchmarks
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the baseline and design 1.5B checkpoints and a mid-training checkpoint on GenEval, DPG-Bench, MMBench, POPE, ImgEdit, GQA, TextVQA, MME and SEED-Bench. Use 5 sampling seeds for generation and greedy decoding for understanding, and report scores with bootstrap intervals over prompts.
CONTROLS: A public 1B reference model; the baseline checkpoint.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: Design scores exceed the baseline by 1 to 3 points on generation sets and stay within 1 point on understanding sets. It could fail if sampling seeds alone move scores by that much.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Placing modality-specific parameters in early, middle or late layers of a 1.5B model
PROPOSAL: Train 1.5B models with 24 layers in which modality-specific feed-forward weights occupy layers 1 to 8, 9 to 16 or 17 to 24, on 30B tokens with 2 seeds. After training, report validation loss per modality, GenEval and MMBench.
CONTROLS: A fully shared model; a model with modality-specific feed-forward weights in all 24 layers; a shared model of equal parameter count with a wider feed-forward.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: Middle placement gives most of the benefit of full separation. It could fail if early layers carry the conflict instead.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sweep over the number of modality-specific layers in a 1.5B model
PROPOSAL: Train 1.5B models with 24 layers in which modality-specific feed-forward weights cover the first 4, 8, 12, 16 or 20 layers, on 60B tokens with 3 seeds, using a shared data order and learning-rate schedule over models. Report validation loss per modality, GenEval and MMBench.
CONTROLS: A fully shared model; a shared model of equal parameter count with a wider feed-forward.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: Validation loss improves up to 8 layers and then flattens. It could fail if the first layers carry most of the conflict.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Instruction-based editing fine-tune of the modality-aware 1.5B model
PROPOSAL: Starting from the pretrained design and baseline 1.5B checkpoints, fine-tune on 300000 editing pairs from SEED-Data-Edit and UltraEdit for 3 epochs, with 3 seeds. Evaluate on ImgEdit-Bench and GEdit-Bench, and measure drift on GenEval and MMBench.
CONTROLS: The baseline checkpoint tuned the same way; tuning with the text part frozen; editing without source-image tokens in the context.
COST: 1100
PREDICTION: The design checkpoint gains 3 to 5 points on ImgEdit-Bench over the baseline with drift under 1 point. It could fail if editing tuning erases the differences between the checkpoints.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: LoRA editing fine-tune of the 1.5B design checkpoint with repeated seeds
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune the pretrained design and baseline 1.5B checkpoints with LoRA of rank 64 on 200000 editing pairs from SEED-Data-Edit, UltraEdit, MagicBrush and InstructPix2Pix, with 5 seeds, and report the spread over seeds. Evaluate on ImgEdit-Bench, GEdit-Bench and MagicBrush test, and measure drift on GenEval.
CONTROLS: The baseline checkpoint tuned the same way; editing without source-image tokens in the context.
COST: 1100
PREDICTION: The design checkpoint gains 2 to 4 points on ImgEdit-Bench over the baseline with drift under 1 point. It could fail if LoRA capacity limits editing quality.
